tasks.description:
Produce the architecture decision that lets Lyra migrate the embedded code-region editor safely, without making this task the feature implementer.

## Observable outcome

A concise written strategy (committed where the team keeps architecture notes) that the migration task consumes, covering: how AvalonEdit's TextEditor replaces the BlockUIContainer-hosted TextBox in EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock; how native caret/mouse selection, the custom Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X fenced copy, and Up/Down arrow boundary-exit navigation re-map from TextBox APIs onto AvalonEdit TextArea/Caret/Document; and how light/dark HighlightingColor palettes are pushed into the editor on each theme switch, given AvalonEdit colors are not WPF DynamicResource-driven.

AvalonEdit colors must be re-applied through a new per-editor hook invoked from MainWindow.ApplyTheme / NotifyThemeChanged rather than relying on SetResourceReference. Keep the editor host and the palette source pluggable so a future Markdown-highlighting reuse is not foreclosed, but do not design or schedule that v2 work.

## Consumers

Tasks 002 and 004 consume this strategy as their integration and theming contract.

tasks.title: Replace region TextBox with AvalonEdit editor
tasks.description:
Stage 1. Replace the plain Consolas TextBox inside EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock with AvalonEdit's TextEditor, introducing the new `ICSharpCode.AvalonEdit` NuGet dependency (first use in the solution), and re-plumb every region behavior currently wired against TextBox APIs. No syntax colors in this stage.

## Observable outcome

Typing three backticks in the prompt RichTextBox still creates an embedded code region, now backed by AvalonEdit, with: working single-click caret placement and caret movement; double-click word selection; click-drag range selection; double-click-drag word-wise extension; the custom Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X fenced copy/cut; Up/Down arrow boundary-exit navigation that leaves the region; TextChanged to Content sync; focus routing into and out of the region; and theme-following background/foreground via the strategy's palette hook (plain editor colors only). The re-plumbed selection gesture must preserve the behavior stabilized in commit 811809a0, including the pure claim predicate (currently ShouldClaimRegionMouseGesture) and the bubbling-stage host-selection collapse in both EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock and MainWindow.PromptTextBox_PreviewMouseLeftButtonDown.

## Serialization

Land the fence serialization convention here: an explicit language serializes as a three-backtick fence followed by the language token; Auto detect serializes as a bare three-backtick fence with no language token; Plain text serializes with the reserved token text. Round-tripping a region must preserve its mode.

## Consumers

The production prompt editor consumes the migrated control. Tasks 003 and 004 build the picker and highlighting on this host; task 007 adds headless regression coverage.

attemptHistory.note:
Defect reported at the Stage 2 human-review gate for the clickable language picker (task -003, commit a0aac71c): clicking an option in the language popup does NOT close the popup and does NOT change the region's language/label/mode. The popup only opens; clicks inside it are inert. Reproduce: open a prompt with an embedded code region, click the language label button to open the picker, then click any option (e.g. 'Plain text' or a grammar) — observe the popup stays open and the label is unchanged.

Root-cause direction (verify, don't assume): the picker Popup is hosted inside the RichTextBox document — it is added to the region header StackPanel via `stack.Children.Add(languagePopup)` in EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock.cs (~line 450), built in BuildLanguagePopup() (EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock.cs ~lines 493-576). Each option Button.Click handler (lines 531-537) already sets `Language = option.FenceToken`, `popup.IsOpen = false`, `_languageButton.Focus()`, so the handler logic is correct but is never invoked. Both symptoms (option Click never fires AND StaysOpen=false never dismisses on outside click) indicate the host RichTextBox is capturing the mouse so pointer events never reach the Popup's separate visual root — a known WPF issue for Popups parented inside a RichTextBox/FlowDocument. The _languageButton.Click toggle works because that button is in the main window visual tree.

Required fix (independently executable): make clicking any picker option (a) dismiss the popup and (b) update the region's Language, _languageLabel text, and PickerMode (raising PickerModeChanged), matching the already-correct option Click body. Likely approaches to evaluate: release/avoid the RichTextBox mouse capture while the popup is open (e.g. call Mouse.Capture(null) or capture to the popup on Opened), and/or re-parent the Popup out of the RichTextBox-hosted StackPanel so it is not inside the document's input-captured surface, and/or handle the option selection on a pointer event that is not swallowed by the host. Preserve: popup still opens below the label (Placement=Bottom, PlacementTarget=_languageButton), StaysOpen=false outside-click dismissal must now actually work, Esc-to-close and Enter/Space-to-select keyboard paths (border.PreviewKeyDown ~lines 556-574) must keep working, selected-item bold/focus on Opened (~lines 540-555) must keep working, and the 811809a0 native-selection behavior and ShouldClaimRegionMouseGesture claim predicate must remain intact. Do not regress the AvalonEdit editor selection/copy/arrow-nav behavior.

Proof: add or extend headless coverage where testable (option-selection write-through to Language/PickerMode/label already has LanguagePicker_OptionClick_WritesFenceAndRoundTripsMode in EmbeddedCodeRegionTests.cs — extend it or add a sibling that also asserts popup dismissal state if reachable headlessly). tasks.title: Highlight built-in grammars with theme-aware palettes
tasks.description:
Stage 3. Apply automatic syntax highlighting for AvalonEdit's standard built-in grammars, with distinct light and dark HighlightingColor palettes, and implement the Auto-detect content heuristic.

## Observable outcome

When a region's mode resolves to a built-in grammar, the editor renders syntax colors. A new per-editor theme hook, invoked from MainWindow.ApplyTheme via NotifyThemeChanged, re-pushes the correct light or dark HighlightingColor palette into every open region editor on each theme switch (AvalonEdit colors are not DynamicResource-driven). Auto-detect resolves the grammar from the fence tag first; when the fence tag is empty it runs a debounced content heuristic after text changes, so while the region is in Auto-detect mode the applied highlighting updates live as the user types. When the user picks Plain text or any explicit language tag, the mode is pinned and the heuristic does not run on further changes.

## Constraints

Keep the palette source pluggable (a future Markdown scheme must be able to register without reworking this engine). Preserve the Stage 1 selection, copy, navigation, and sync behavior.

## Consumers

The production region editor consumes the highlighting engine, theme hook, and auto-detect engine. Tasks 005 and 006 register custom grammars and palettes through the same engine and hook; task 008 covers the heuristic and pinning logic headlessly.

tasks.title: Bundle custom grammars: Go, Rust, Bash, Markdown
tasks.description:
Stage 5. Add and bundle custom AvalonEdit .xshd highlighting grammars for Go, Rust, Bash, and Markdown, registered with the picker list, the highlighting engine, and the light/dark palette hook.

## Observable outcome

Each of Go, Rust, Bash, and Markdown appears in the language picker and, when selected or auto-detected, renders its own syntax highlighting with correct light and dark colors in a region. The grammars load from embedded resources without runtime exceptions.

## Consumers

The production region editor and picker consume the four new grammars through the existing engine and hook. The following human validation gate uses copy-ready sample snippets to confirm per-language color correctness and allows iterative palette tuning. Keep the Markdown grammar registration path reusable, but add no further v2 Markdown-editor work.

approvalGates.message: Stage 2 review: confirm the language-label picker opens directly below the label and updates the region mode
approvalGates.lastReworkInstructions:
Defect reported at the Stage 2 human-review gate for the clickable language picker (task -003, commit a0aac71c): clicking an option in the language popup does NOT close the popup and does NOT change the region's language/label/mode. The popup only opens; clicks inside it are inert. Reproduce: open a prompt with an embedded code region, click the language label button to open the picker, then click any option (e.g. 'Plain text' or a grammar) — observe the popup stays open and the label is unchanged.

Root-cause direction (verify, don't assume): the picker Popup is hosted inside the RichTextBox document — it is added to the region header StackPanel via `stack.Children.Add(languagePopup)` in EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock.cs (~line 450), built in BuildLanguagePopup() (EmbeddedCodeRegionBlock.cs ~lines 493-576). Each option Button.Click handler (lines 531-537) already sets `Language = option.FenceToken`, `popup.IsOpen = false`, `_languageButton.Focus()`, so the handler logic is correct but is never invoked. Both symptoms (option Click never fires AND StaysOpen=false never dismisses on outside click) indicate the host RichTextBox is capturing the mouse so pointer events never reach the Popup's separate visual root — a known WPF issue for Popups parented inside a RichTextBox/FlowDocument. The _languageButton.Click toggle works because that button is in the main window visual tree.

Required fix (independently executable): make clicking any picker option (a) dismiss the popup and (b) update the region's Language, _languageLabel text, and PickerMode (raising PickerModeChanged), matching the already-correct option Click body. Likely approaches to evaluate: release/avoid the RichTextBox mouse capture while the popup is open (e.g. call Mouse.Capture(null) or capture to the popup on Opened), and/or re-parent the Popup out of the RichTextBox-hosted StackPanel so it is not inside the document's input-captured surface, and/or handle the option selection on a pointer event that is not swallowed by the host. Preserve: popup still opens below the label (Placement=Bottom, PlacementTarget=_languageButton), StaysOpen=false outside-click dismissal must now actually work, Esc-to-close and Enter/Space-to-select keyboard paths (border.PreviewKeyDown ~lines 556-574) must keep working, selected-item bold/focus on Opened (~lines 540-555) must keep working, and the 811809a0 native-selection behavior and ShouldClaimRegionMouseGesture claim predicate must remain intact. Do not regress the AvalonEdit editor selection/copy/arrow-nav behavior.

Proof: add or extend headless coverage where testable (option-selection write-through to Language/PickerMode/label already has LanguagePicker_OptionClick_WritesFenceAndRoundTripsMode in EmbeddedCodeRegionTests.cs — extend it or add a sibling that also asserts popup dismissal state if reachable headlessly). Rebuild SquadDash.csproj green and re-run the filtered EmbeddedCodeRegion/EmbeddedCaretNav suite. Because popup dismissal and label update are human-observable, this returns to the Stage 2 human gate: the reviewer must confirm that clicking a picker item closes the popup and the region label updates to the chosen mode.

approvalGates.message: Stage 3 review: confirm built-in-grammar highlighting, light/dark correctness, live auto-detect, and pinned Plain text
approvalGates.lastReworkInstructions: Fix the Stage 3 defect where live auto-detect highlighting never applies to recognizable code. Root cause: SquadDash/RegionGrammarResolver.cs DetectBuiltIn (lines ~164-193) recognizes C# only via four narrow Tier-2 markers (RegionGrammarResolver.cs:73-79): '\busing\s+System\b', '\bnamespace\s+...;' (semicolon form only), '\bConsole\.(Write|WriteLine)\b', and '\bpublic\s+static\s+void\s+Main\s*\(\s*string\[\]'. Ordinary declaration-style C# — e.g. the reviewer's samples 'public interface ICalloutWindow { event EventHandler? RefreshTargetRect; bool ShowDiagnostics { get; set; } void UpdateTargetRect(Rect rect); double LastDragAngle { get; } }' and 'public class MainWindow { }' — matches none of these, so DetectBuiltIn returns null, Resolve returns no grammar, and the region never leaves plain text in Auto detect. The debounce/timer/RefreshHighlighting wiring (AvalonEditRegionEditor.cs:49-106) is functioning; only the classifier is too narrow. WORK (production owner: lyra-morn; test owner: vesper-knox): (1) In RegionGrammarResolver, broaden the C# Tier-2 markers so realistic declaration-style C# is classified as 'C#' while keeping the existing conservative single-winner ambiguity rule (two or more Tier-2 language matches must still return null). Add C#-distinctive signals that do NOT also fire the Java/C++/JavaScript markers, for example: brace-form 'namespace [A-Za-z_][\w.]*\s*\{'; a C# using directive 'using [A-Za-z_][\w.]*\s*;' that is not 'import'/'package'; auto-property accessor lists '\{\s*get\b' / 'set;'; 'event\s+\w'; nullable reference/value type usage like 'EventHandler?' or a '\w+\?\s+\w+' field/return type; and access-modified type declarations '(public|private|protected|internal)\s+(sealed\s+|abstract\s+|static\s+|partial\s+)*(class|interface|struct|record|enum)\b'. Because Java also uses 'public class', ensure C#-only signals (nullable '?', '{ get; set; }', 'event', 'namespace {', 'using X;' without 'java.') are what tip the single-winner selection to C#, and verify a plain 'public class Foo {}' with no other signals still resolves deterministically (either to C# via an added marker or to null) without throwing or double-counting. Keep MaxScanLength, NonBacktracking RegexOptions, and the Tier-1 PHP/XML/HTML document-signature precedence unchanged. (2) Do not weaken PlainText pinning: Resolve must still return null for the 'text' token and SetLanguage must still stop the auto-detect timer. (3) Regression tests in SquadDash.Tests (RegionGrammarResolverTests.cs): assert DetectBuiltIn returns 'C#' for BOTH reviewer samples verbatim; assert at least one additional realistic C# snippet (class with { get; set; } properties and a method) resolves to 'C#'; assert a deliberately ambiguous/prose sample still returns null; and assert Java ('import java.util.List; public class X { public static void main(String[] a){} }'), JavaScript ('console.log(1)'), and C++ ('#include <vector>') still resolve to their own grammars (no C# false-positive). Extend or add an AvalonEditRegionEditor-level test confirming that, in Auto detect mode, applying one of the reviewer samples as text causes RefreshHighlighting to set a non-null SyntaxHighlighting named 'C#' (fence token empty). (4) Build green with ONLY env DOTNET_MSBUILD_SDK_RESOLVER_CLI_DIR set (do not also set MSBuildExtensionsPath) and run 'dotnet test SquadDash.Tests\SquadDash.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~RegionGrammar|FullyQualifiedName~Highlight|FullyQualifiedName~AutoDetect|FullyQualifiedName~EmbeddedCodeRegion"'; report exact pass counts. Commit test + production changes to the already-prepared branch feature/avalonedit-region-editor (do not create or switch branches). After the amendment lands, the Stage 3 gate must be re-tested by the human: paste each reviewer sample into an Auto detect region and confirm live C# highlighting appears, then select Plain text and confirm highlighting stops changing while typing.
